A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AxBench study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Appendix renumbering and reorganized displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-detection and steering experiments, plus appendix studies of data efficiency, generated steering vectors, cross-model transfer, and SAE interventions.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical studies and reports revised steering results, a new bag-of-words comparison, and additional SAE-A evaluations.

M1.justification: The synthetic-data pipeline and core ReFT-r1 procedure remain: concept detection through a learned direction, top-k-dependent intervention training, and language-modeling loss with sparsity regularization. The equation corrections and newly documented optimization details do not establish an underlying algorithm change. Generated-vector and affine-transfer methods already appear in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use CONCEPT10, CONCEPT500, CONCEPT16K, the same text/code/math instruction sources, and Alpaca-Eval steering instructions. Balanced and imbalanced detection, cross-model transfer, and English/Chinese examples are retained; the added comparator introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds BoW to the main detection and imbalance comparisons and adds SAE-A results for both Gemma-2-9B layers in Tables 1–3. Conversely, generated-vector and affine-transfer comparisons shrink from broad baseline lists in v1 Tables 4–7 to ReFT-r1, DiffMean, and SAE in v3 Tables 4–5, removing prompting and finetuning comparators from those comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 divides the ten steering instructions per concept equally between steering-factor selection and held-out evaluation; v1 selects the factor maximizing the evaluation score without this separation. Prompting and finetuning also change from averaging factor-indexed generations to randomly scoring a generation on the testing instructions, equalizing sampling with steering methods. These substantially revise the central evaluation design.

E4.justification: BoW is added to the existing balanced-versus-imbalanced detection analysis. The data-scaling, generated-vector, affine-transfer, and SAE clamping studies remain, with revised steering outcomes rather than new analytical questions. The code-error clustering example also replaces one highlighted feature.

E5.justification: Both retain paired t-test reporting in Section 5.1, existing error-bar and distribution displays, and three data-scaling seeds, 42, 43, and 44. No new uncertainty estimator or increased replication count is reported. Condensed appendix tables omit duplicated significance markings that remain available in the main comparison.

E6.justification: Under the revised steering protocol, Table 2 replaces ReFT-r1's mean score of 0.735 with 0.543 and SAE's 0.315 with 0.165; ReFT-r1 moves from third to fifth. Table 3 changes ReFT-r1's mean win rate from 88.0% to 81.8%. v3 also adds BoW AUROC results, averaging 0.914, and 9B SAE-A entries, while updating generated-vector, transfer, scaling, and clamping results. These are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation 9 corrects the ReFT-r1 intervention to add the mean top-k activation multiplied by the learned vector to each token representation. The appendix clamping equations now subtract the original latent activation, including for minimum clamping. These correct mathematical definitions; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: AxBench enables large-scale comparison, simple baselines outperform SAEs, and ReFT-r1 helps close the steering gap while supporting concept detection. These claims are not substantively reframed despite the revised results.

C2.justification: Section 6 strengthens the qualification concerning SAE labels. v1 notes shallow concepts and possible changes in benchmark rankings; v3 explicitly attributes part of SAE underperformance to limitations of automatic interpretation, even after supervised feature selection, and suggests better labeling could improve SAE performance.

D1.justification: v3 documents removal of gradients parallel to learned weights for Probe and ReFT-r1, specifies equally weighted MSE and cosine losses for the affine mapper, and supplies BoW tokenization and hyperparameter grids. These are additional implementation disclosures; the original unit-norm constraint, prompt templates, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bhalla et al. (2025) to the discussion of interpretability-based control and previous steering evaluations. The broader positioning and historical appendix remain substantially unchanged; other reference edits mainly concern bibliographic formatting.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and notation edits, moves the SAE concept-source footnote into Appendix B, consolidates the SAE ablation subsections, and adds an Impact Statements section. The main narrative, section order, and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The mean ROC plot moves from the main text to the appendix, comparison displays expand for BoW and 9B SAE-A, Figure 10 gains connecting lines, and Figure 11 is redesigned with a labeled cluster enlargement. Four large supplementary comparison tables become two compact paired tables, and hyperparameter tables gain BoW columns and rows. This substantially reorganizes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The held-out steering-factor evaluation and matched generation sampling address an important source of optimistic and uneven comparisons in v1's central benchmark. Corrected intervention equations and additional controls further strengthen validity and reproducibility. Reporting remains imperfect: Section 5.2 still quotes win rates of 88.0% and 61.6%, although Table 3 now reports 81.8% and 58.7%, and retains optimistic ReFT-r1 comparison prose. These inconsistencies temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial evaluation improvement.
